You can paste this as a prompt or hand this file as an .md to treat it as a skill. Prompt: You are building a production web interface. The rules below are constraints, not suggestions. When a rule conflicts with what you were about to generate, the rule wins. The goal is not "avoid a list of things." It is to make a deliberate choice in each place where the default would be decoration. If you remove a banned element and put nothing considered in its place, the result is worse, not better. 1. Colour ● Choose ONE accent colour. Everything else is neutral, a single family of greys with a consistent temperature (all warm or all cool, never mixed). ● A second colour is allowed only when it carries meaning: destructive, success, warning. Never for variety. ● Banned: blue→purple and indigo→violet gradients, anywhere. That means backgrounds, buttons, headings, logos, icons, borders, blurred "blobs", mesh backgrounds. ● Banned: gradient text (background-clip: text). Headings are one solid colour. ● Banned: giving each feature, category, or section its own hue. A feature grid uses the same colour for every card. Colour encodes meaning; it is not decoration. ● Do not ship a framework's default palette untouched (Tailwind indigo/violet/slate is the single most recognisable generated-site signature). Define your own tokens. ● Accent usage target: under 10% of the visible surface. If the page looks colourful, you have overused it. 2. Depth and separation ● Banned: a drop shadow on anything that is not genuinely floating above the page. Cards, sections, images, inputs, badges, and static buttons get no shadow. ● Shadows are permitted only on elements that truly overlay: dropdowns, popovers, modals, toasts. Keep them tight and low-opacity. A real one reads as 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.06), not a 40px purple bloom. ● Separate blocks with a 1px border, a background step, or whitespace, in that order of preference. Whitespace is the best separator and costs nothing. ● Do not stack multiple shadows on one element to simulate depth. ● Pick one border-radius value and one border colour, and use them everywhere. 3. Icons and emoji ● Banned: the sparkle icon. ✨ ✦ ✧ 🪄 and every "AI shimmer" glyph, in buttons, badges, logos, nav, headings, or beside a product name. The sparkle-as-AI is the single clearest tell there is. If a feature uses AI, say so in words. ● Banned: emoji used as UI. No emoji in headings, buttons, feature lists, badges, navigation, or empty states. Not 🚀 , not ⚡ , not 🎯 , not 🔥 . Emoji are user content, never interface. ● Banned: any container around an icon. No tinted rounded square, no circle, no bordered box, no coloured chip behind it. The icon sits directly on the background at text size. The icon-in-a-soft-tinted-square is a template signature. ● Use one real icon set (Lucide, Heroicons, Phosphor) at one stroke weight. Monochrome, inheriting currentColor, sized to the text beside it. ● If a feature is clear from its label, it does not need an icon at all. 4. Typography and copy ● Banned words, in copy and in headings: unleash, supercharge, elevate, transform, revolutionise, empower, seamless, effortless, effortlessly, cutting-edge, game-changing, next-level, unlock, harness, robust, leverage, powerful, delve, paradigm, synergy. If a sentence survives deleting the adjective, delete the adjective. ● Banned: the em dash (—) in UI copy. It is the strongest text-level tell. Write two sentences, or use a comma. This applies to headings, body, tooltips, and empty states. ● Say what the product does, in concrete nouns and real numbers. "Export to CSV in one click" beats "Seamlessly unlock your data's potential." ● One type family (two at most: UI and mono). A real scale, roughly 12 / 14 / 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 48. No sizes between steps. ● Body text is left-aligned. Centre only short headings. Never centre a paragraph over three lines. Cap measure at ~70 characters. ● Sentence case for headings and buttons. No Title Case Everywhere, no ALL-CAPS except tiny labels with tracking. 5. Motion ● Banned: an arrow inside a button that slides on hover. Also banned: arrows that animate on their own, bouncing chevrons, and any looping idle motion. ● Banned: hover glow. No box-shadow bloom, no coloured halo, no scale() above 1.02, no lift on hover for cards or buttons. ● Hover states change background or border colour only, at 120–160ms ease-out. ● Animate opacity and transform only. Duration 120–200ms for UI feedback, up to 300ms for something entering. Nothing eases for half a second. ● No scroll-triggered fade-ins on every section. No parallax. No typewriter, no counters ticking up, no marquee of logos. ● Honour prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and disable non-essential motion inside it. 6. Scale and proportion Nothing is oversized. Everything is sized to its content and fits neatly. Inflated type, padding and buttons are how a generated page announces itself before you read a word. ● Hero headline: 40–56px on desktop, 28–34px on mobile. Never 72px+. A headline does not need to fill the screen to be the headline. ● Body text 15–16px. Secondary text 13–14px. Nothing below 12px. ● Buttons 36–44px tall, with padding sized to the label, not to make a statement. Never full-width on desktop. A primary and a secondary button are enough. ● Section padding 64–96px vertical on desktop, 40–56px on mobile. Not 160px+. ● Content max-width 1100–1280px. Text columns capped at ~65–70 characters. Do not let a line of text run the full width of a 1920px monitor. ● Inline icons 16–20px, standalone icons 24px. No 48px+ decorative icons. ● No section is a full viewport tall just for impact. The hero should show that content continues below it. ● Cards are sized by their content. Force equal heights only when the content really is equal; otherwise let them differ. ● Every spacing value is a multiple of 4. Elements in a row share their top and bottom edges. Related items align to the same left edge. Neatness is alignment plus consistent spacing, nothing more. 7. Layout and structure ● Banned: the eyebrow badge. No pill above the hero reading "Introducing v2.0", "AI-Powered", "New", or "Trusted by developers". If it were important it would be in the headline. ● Do not reproduce the default template order (hero → logo strip → three features → testimonial → three pricing tiers → FAQ → repeated CTA). Build only the sections this product actually needs, in the order a real user needs them. ● Feature grids do not have to be three columns of equal-length cards. Let real content set the shape; uneven is fine, and reads as human. ● Not everything is centred. Not everything is a card. Not every corner is fully rounded. ● One spacing scale (4px base). Vertical rhythm should be visibly consistent; a generated page usually has arbitrary gaps between every section. 8. Placeholder content ● Mockup content is fine. Logo strips, "Trusted by 10,000+ teams", sample testimonials and example metrics all belong in a demo build. Do not leave sections empty waiting for real copy. ● What gives a page away is not that the content is placeholder, it is that the placeholder is generic. Make it specific: named companies rather than "Company A", a testimonial that mentions an actual feature, a number that is oddly precise rather than a round 10,000+. ● Placeholder copy still obeys section 4. No hype adjectives, no em dashes, no emoji. ● Write real empty states, error states, and loading states. Their absence is what makes a build feel unfinished. 9. Code craft ● Semantic HTML: header, nav, main, section, button, a. A clickable div is a bug. ● Real, visible :focus-visible styles. Keyboard order must match visual order. ● Every image has meaningful alt; decorative images get alt="". ● Colour contrast at least 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text. ● Reuse components instead of pasting a block with different text. If the same markup appears three times, extract it. ● Use design tokens or theme values, not one-off arbitrary values scattered per element. ● No dead code, no commented-out blocks, no unused imports, no placeholder TODOs in a delivered file. Before you say it is finished Go through every line. Fix what fails. 1. Any blue→purple or indigo→violet gradient left, anywhere? 2. Any gradient text? 3. Does anything that is not floating still have a shadow? 4. Any sparkle glyph, anywhere? 5. Any emoji used as interface? 6. Does any icon sit inside a tinted square, circle, or box? 7. Any em dash in the copy? 8. Any hits from the banned word list? 9. Does each feature or category have its own colour? 10. Does any button contain a moving arrow? 11. Does anything glow, lift, or scale on hover? 12. Is there a badge above the hero that says nothing? 13. Is the hero headline above 56px, or any section over 96px of vertical padding? 14. Does any element look oversized next to the text beside it? If a reviewer could tell this was generated in under five seconds, find the specific thing that gave it away and fix that.

description: Enforces authentic, production-grade UI design rules and eliminates generic AI aesthetic tropes (no purple gradients, no sparkles, no decorative shadows, restrained typography, semantic HTML, and RTL compatibility). # Anti-AI Slop Design System & Craft Guidelines

You are building a production web interface. The rules below are hard constraints, not suggestions. When a rule conflicts with what you were about to generate or what a default template provides, **the rule wins**.

The goal is not simply to "avoid a list of things." It is to make a deliberate, craft-focused choice in each place where the default would otherwise be mindless decoration. If you remove a banned element and put nothing considered in its place, the result is worse, not better.

---

## 1. Colour Tokens & Accent Discipline

- **One Accent Colour:** Choose exactly ONE accent colour for the entire interface. Everything else is neutral, drawn from a single family of greys with a consistent temperature (all warm or all cool, never mixed).
- **Semantic Secondary Colours Only:** A second colour is allowed only when it carries objective functional meaning: destructive/error (red), success (green), warning (amber). Never introduce a colour for variety or novelty.
- **Banned Gradients:** Blue-to-purple (`#2563eb` → `#9333ea`) and indigo-to-violet gradients are strictly forbidden anywhere. This includes backgrounds, buttons, headings, logos, icons, borders, blurred "blobs", and mesh backgrounds.
- **Banned Gradient Text:** Gradient text (`background-clip: text` with transparent fill) is banned. All headings and text must be solid, high-contrast colours.
- **Unified Feature Palette:** Banned: giving each feature, category, or card its own distinct hue (e.g. rainbow card decks). A feature grid must use the exact same neutral surface and colour scheme across all cards. Colour encodes meaning, not decorative variety.
- **No Untouched Framework Palettes:** Do not ship Tailwind's default palette untouched (`indigo-600`, `violet-500`, `slate-900` is the single most recognizable AI signature). Define deliberate, project-specific design tokens.
- **Accent Surface Budget:** Keep accent colour usage strictly under 10% of the visible surface area. If a page looks colourful at a glance, the accent colour has been overused.

---

## 2. Depth, Surfaces & Shadows

- **No Fake Shadows:** A drop shadow is banned on anything that is not genuinely floating in the viewport z-axis. Cards, sections, containers, images, input fields, badges, and static buttons get zero shadow (`box-shadow: none`).
- **Permitted Shadows (Overlays Only):** Shadows are permitted exclusively on elements that physically overlay page content: dropdown menus, popovers, dialogs/modals, and toast notifications.
- **Tight, Subtle Elevation:** When a shadow is permitted, keep it tight and low-opacity (e.g. `0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06)` or `0 4px 12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08)`). A 40px coloured bloom is strictly banned. Never stack multiple shadows to simulate fake depth.
- **Real Separation Hierarchy:** Separate blocks and cards using the following order of preference:
  1. Whitespace (the best separator, zero visual noise).
  2. A subtle 1px border (`border: 1px solid var(--border)`).
  3. A single background step (`bg-neutral-50` vs `bg-white` or `neutral-900` vs `neutral-950`).
- **Consistent Radius and Border:** Pick exactly one border-radius value (e.g. `6px` or `8px`) and one border colour, and apply them consistently across all inputs, cards, and buttons.

---

## 3. Icons, Glyphs & Emoji

- **Banned AI Shimmer & Sparkles:** The sparkle icon (`✨`, `✦`, `✧`, `🪄`) and any "AI shimmer" glyph are banned across buttons, badges, logos, navigation, headings, and beside product names. The sparkle-as-AI icon is the clearest indicator of an AI-generated site. If a feature uses machine learning or automation, describe what it does in plain words.
- **Banned Emoji as Interface:** Emoji are banned in headings, buttons, feature lists, badges, tabs, navigation, or empty states (no `🚀`, `⚡`, `🎯`, `🔥`, `💡`). Emoji belong in user content, never in a production interface.
- **No Icon Container Chips:** Any container around an icon is banned. No tinted rounded squares, no pastel circles, no bordered boxes, no coloured background chips behind icons. The icon sits directly on the background at text size. The icon-in-a-soft-tinted-square is an overused template signature.
- **Unified Icon System:** Use a single production icon set (Lucide, Heroicons, or Phosphor) with a consistent stroke weight (typically 1.5px or 1.75px). Render icons in monochrome inheriting `currentColor`, sized proportionally to the adjacent text.
- **Label Clarity First:** If a feature or button is self-evident from its label, omit the icon entirely.

---

## 4. Typography, Measure & Copywriting

- **Banned AI Buzzwords:** The following words are banned in both UI copy and marketing headings:
  > *unleash, supercharge, elevate, transform, revolutionise, empower, seamless, effortless, effortlessly, cutting-edge, game-changing, next-level, unlock, harness, robust, leverage, powerful, delve, paradigm, synergy.*
  > 
  > *Rule of thumb:* If a sentence survives deleting the adjective, delete the adjective.
- **Banned Em Dash in UI:** The em dash (`—`) is banned in UI copy, microcopy, headings, tooltips, and empty states. Write two distinct sentences, or use a comma or parentheses.
- **Concrete Nouns & Real Numbers:** State what the product actually does. Example: *"Export transactions to CSV in one click"* beats *"Seamlessly unlock your financial data's full potential."*
- **Typographic Scale:** Limit the project to one type family (at most two: one UI sans-serif, one monospace for data/code). Adhere to a strict, stepped scale: `12 / 14 / 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 48px`. Avoid arbitrary intermediate sizes.
- **Alignment & Reading Measure:** Body text must be aligned to the reading start (left-aligned for LTR, right-aligned for RTL). Center only short headings (1-2 lines). Never center a paragraph longer than three lines. Cap body text measure at ~65-75 characters per line (`max-w-prose` / `max-width: 65ch`).
- **Sentence Case:** Use sentence case for headings, labels, and buttons. Avoid Title Case Everywhere, and never use ALL-CAPS except for tracked micro-labels (`tracking-wider text-xs uppercase`).

---

## 5. Motion, States & Transitions

- **Banned Button Animations:** An arrow inside a button that slides on hover is banned. Bouncing chevrons, arrows that animate on their own, and looping idle motions are banned.
- **Banned Hover Effects:** Hover glow, box-shadow blooms, coloured halos, `scale()` transforms above 1.02, and card-lifting hover transitions are banned.
- **Clean Interactive States:** Hover states should change background or border colour only, using a subtle duration of 120-160ms with `ease-out`.
- **Restrained Animation Properties:** Animate `opacity` and `transform` exclusively. Durations: 120-200ms for UI feedback, up to 300ms for entering dialogs or drawers. Avoid easing curves lasting 500ms or longer.
- **No Scroll Gimmicks:** No scroll-triggered fade-ins on every section. No parallax backgrounds. No typewriter effects, no ticking-up numbers, no infinite marquee strips of company logos.
- **Respect Motion Preferences:** Always wrap animations in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` to disable or flatten non-essential motion.

---

## 6. Scale, Proportions & 4px Rhythm

Nothing should be oversized. Everything must be sized to fit its content neatly. Inflated typography, padding, and buttons announce an automated template before a single word is read.

- **Hero Headline:** 40-56px on desktop, 28-34px on mobile. Never 72px+. A headline does not need to fill the entire viewport height to be impactful.
- **Body & Secondary Text:** Body text is 15-16px. Secondary/caption text is 13-14px. Nothing readable below 12px.
- **Button Sizing:** 36-44px tall, with horizontal padding sized to the text label. Never full-width on desktop. A primary button and a secondary outline/ghost button are sufficient.
- **Section Vertical Padding:** 64-96px on desktop, 40-56px on mobile. Avoid massive 160px+ empty vertical gaps.
- **Container Max-Width:** 1100-1280px maximum. Never allow a line of text or card grid to stretch across the full width of an ultrawide or 1920px screen.
- **Icon Sizing:** Inline icons 16-20px; standalone feature icons 24px. No 48px+ decorative floating icons.
- **No Full-Viewport Hero Trap:** Avoid forcing the hero section to `100vh` just for dramatic effect. The hero must visually hint that real content continues below the fold.
- **Card Heights:** Cards must be sized by their internal content. Do not force artificial equal heights unless the content items are genuinely identical.
- **4px Spatial Grid:** Every margin, padding, gap, and dimension must be a multiple of 4px (`4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64px`). Align related elements to consistent start and baseline edges.

---

## 7. Layout Structure & Template Cliché Elimination

- **Banned Eyebrow Pill Badge:** Banned: the generic pill badge floating above the hero headline reading *"Introducing v2.0"*, *"AI-Powered"*, *"New"*, or *"Trusted by 10,000+ developers"*. If a piece of information is critical, place it directly in the headline; if not, remove it.
- **Break the Cliché Template Sequence:** Do not blindly generate the standard sequence:
  > *Hero → Monochromatic logo strip → 3 feature cards → 1 customer quote → 3 pricing tiers → Accordion FAQ → Repeated CTA banner.*
  
  Build only the specific sections this product actually requires, in the logical sequence a prospective user or operator needs to evaluate it.
- **Organic Content-Driven Grids:** Feature layouts do not have to be rigid 3-column cards of identical length. Let real data, metrics, code snippets, or workflows determine card geometry.
- **Restraint Over Uniformity:** Not every container needs to be a bordered card, not every layout needs to be centered, and not every corner needs full rounding.

---

## 8. Specific Placeholder & Edge States

- **Specific Over Generic Placeholders:** If demo content is needed, avoid generic placeholders like *"Acme Corp"*, *"Company A"*, or generic stock names. Use plausible, industry-specific names, realistic testimonial text referencing concrete workflows, and natural, non-round numbers (e.g. `99.94%` or `1,420` instead of `10,000+`).
- **Placeholder Copy Discipline:** Placeholder copy must obey all typography rules: no hype adjectives, no em dashes, and no emoji.
- **First-Class Edge States:** Every UI surface must include well-designed, functional edge states:
  - Empty states (with a clear, single-click action to create or import).
  - Error states (actionable explanation with recovery paths).
  - Loading skeletons (restrained, matching the exact shape of incoming content).

---

## 9. Code Craft, Accessibility & RTL Support

- **Semantic HTML Only:** Use semantic tags (`<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<section>`, `<article>`, `<button>`, `<a>`). A clickable `<div>` or `<span>` without button semantics and keyboard handlers is a critical bug.
- **Visible Focus States:** Provide clear, high-contrast `:focus-visible` styling on all interactive elements. Ensure keyboard navigation order mirrors the visual layout.
- **Image Accessibility:** Every informative image must feature descriptive `alt` text. Purely decorative elements must have `alt=""` and `aria-hidden="true"`.
- **WCAG Contrast Ratios:** Ensure contrast ratios reach at least 4.5:1 for standard body text and 3:1 for large text and interactive boundaries.
- **Component Hygiene:** Extract repeated markup into reusable components if it appears three or more times. Rely on design tokens or CSS custom properties, never arbitrary one-off inline values.
- **Full BiDi & RTL Support:**
  - Use CSS Logical Properties (`margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline-end`, `inset-inline-start`, `text-align: start`) instead of physical `left` and `right`.
  - When rendering Arabic text, ensure `dir="rtl"` is set, text is right-aligned (`text-align: right/start`), and Western digits or Latin symbols are isolated (`<bdi>` or `dir="ltr"`).

---

## 10. Pre-Completion Audit Checklist

Before declaring any UI task or component complete, review every line against these 14 audit questions:

| # | Inspection Question | Status |
|---|---------------------|:------:|
| 1 | Is there any blue-to-purple or indigo-to-violet gradient anywhere? | Must be NO |
| 2 | Is there any gradient text (`background-clip: text`)? | Must be NO |
| 3 | Does anything that is not a floating overlay (modal, popover, toast) have a shadow? | Must be NO |
| 4 | Is there any sparkle, star, or AI shimmer glyph (`✨`, `✦`, `🪄`)? | Must be NO |
| 5 | Is any emoji used as an interface element, icon, or badge? | Must be NO |
| 6 | Does any icon sit inside a tinted square, circle, or coloured background chip? | Must be NO |
| 7 | Is there any em dash (`—`) in UI copy or microcopy? | Must be NO |
| 8 | Does the copy contain any banned buzzwords (*unleash, supercharge, seamless, etc.*)? | Must be NO |
| 9 | Does each card or category have its own decorative colour hue? | Must be NO |
| 10 | Does any button contain a sliding arrow or bouncy animation on hover? | Must be NO |
| 11 | Does any card or button glow, lift, or scale on hover? | Must be NO |
| 12 | Is there an empty eyebrow pill badge above the hero? | Must be NO |
| 13 | Is the hero headline over 56px, or does any section have vertical padding over 96px? | Must be NO |
| 14 | Does any element look disproportionately oversized relative to its adjacent content? | Must be NO |

If a reviewer could identify that the page was generated by AI in under five seconds, pinpoint the exact telltale pattern and replace it with intentional, production-grade craft.

If a sentence survives deleting the adjective, delete the adjective.

# Anti-AI Slop: Production Web Interface Design Rules & Skill

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Skills Compatibility](https://img.shields.io/badge/Skills-Antigravity%20%7C%20Claude%20Code%20%7C%20Cursor%20%7C%20Windsurf-success.svg)](#installation)

> **Eliminate the telltale signs of AI-generated web templates. Enforce restrained, intentional, production-grade craft.**
>
> **دليل ومهارة تصميم برمجية لمنع مخرجات الذكاء الاصطناعي النمطية (AI Slop) وإنتاج واجهات ويب حقيقية واحترافية.**

---

## The Problem (المشكلة)

When modern AI models generate web interfaces, they suffer from deep statistical biases that make the output immediately recognizable within seconds:
- **Blue-to-purple and indigo-to-violet gradients** on every button, background, and text header.
- **Sparkles and shimmers (`✨`, `✦`, `🪄`)** sprinkled across every feature and badge.
- **Inflated hype copy:** *"Unleash"*, *"Supercharge"*, *"Seamlessly unlock your full potential"*.
- **Heavy decorative drop-shadows** and rainbow-coloured card grids.
- **Icons imprisoned in tinted pastel rounded squares**.
- **Rigid boilerplate structures:** *Hero → Logo strip → 3 cards → Quote → 3 pricing tiers → FAQ*.

The result is "AI Slop" — interfaces that look like cheap templates and erode user trust.

---

## The Solution (الحل)

This repository provides **strict, non-negotiable craft constraints** that replace decorative defaults with deliberate, production-ready human decisions (similar to software built by Stripe, Linear, and Vercel).

Available in two formats:
1. **`SKILL.md`**: An autonomous **Agent Skill** compatible with Google Antigravity, Claude Code, and agentic workflows. It triggers automatically whenever you design, style, or review frontend code.
2. **`DESIGN_RULES.md`**: A standalone reference document to drop into project roots, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, or `.cursorrules`.

---

## Core Rules at a Glance (أبرز القواعد)

| Domain | Rule | Banned Tropes |
|---|---|---|
| **Colour** | 1 accent colour (<10% surface). Single neutral family. | Purple/indigo gradients, gradient text, rainbow feature grids. |
| **Depth** | 1px borders, subtle background steps, whitespace. | Drop-shadows on cards/inputs/buttons (shadows only on real modals/popovers). |
| **Icons & Emoji** | Monochrome icons at text size inheriting `currentColor`. | Sparkles (`✨`), emoji in UI (🚀, ⚡), icons in tinted pastel rounded boxes. |
| **Typography** | Concrete nouns, real numbers, 1-2 type families, 12-48px scale. | Buzzwords (*supercharge, unleash, seamless*), em dashes (`—`) in UI copy. |
| **Motion** | Restrained 120-160ms ease-out transitions on border/color. | Sliding button arrows, hover glow/halo/scale, bouncy chevrons, idle loops. |
| **Scale** | Hero headline 40-56px desktop. 4px spatial rhythm. | 72px+ giant headlines, 160px+ padding, full-viewport `100vh` hero traps. |
| **Layout** | Content-driven grid shapes and natural section flow. | Generic eyebrow pill badges (*"Introducing v2.0"*), cookie-cutter template orders. |
| **Placeholders** | Specific company names, precise metrics, real empty/error states. | Generic *"Company A"*, round *"10,000+"* placeholders, missing edge states. |
| **Code Craft** | Semantic HTML, accessible `:focus-visible`, logical CSS (RTL/LTR). | Clickable `<div>`, unlabelled images, arbitrary inline values, low contrast. |

---

## Installation & Usage (طريقة التثبيت والاستخدام)

### Option 1: Antigravity / Gemini CLI (`agy`)

To install globally for all your projects:

#### Windows (PowerShell):
```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "$HOME\.gemini\config\skills\anti-ai-slop"
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<YOUR_USERNAME>/anti-ai-slop/main/SKILL.md" -OutFile "$HOME\.gemini\config\skills\anti-ai-slop\SKILL.md"
```

#### macOS / Linux:
```bash
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config/skills/anti-ai-slop
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<YOUR_USERNAME>/anti-ai-slop/main/SKILL.md -o ~/.gemini/config/skills/anti-ai-slop/SKILL.md
```

Once installed, Antigravity will automatically load and enforce the skill whenever you build or edit UI components.

---

### Option 2: Claude Code

Add as a personal skill:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/anti-ai-slop
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<YOUR_USERNAME>/anti-ai-slop/main/SKILL.md -o ~/.claude/skills/anti-ai-slop/SKILL.md
```

Or append the rules directly to your global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`:
```bash
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<YOUR_USERNAME>/anti-ai-slop/main/DESIGN_RULES.md >> ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
```

---

### Option 3: Cursor, Windsurf, or VS Code

Place `DESIGN_RULES.md` in your project root, or copy its content into `.cursorrules` / `.windsurfrules`:

```bash
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<YOUR_USERNAME>/anti-ai-slop/main/DESIGN_RULES.md -o .cursorrules
```

---

### Option 4: Direct Prompting (v0, ChatGPT, Claude.ai, Gemini)

Copy the raw text of [`DESIGN_RULES.md`](DESIGN_RULES.md) and paste it at the beginning of your prompt:

```text
You are building a production web interface. The following rules are hard constraints, not suggestions...
[Paste DESIGN_RULES.md here]
```

---

## Pre-Completion Audit Checklist (قائمة التحقق قبل التسليم)

Before shipping any UI code, review against these 14 audit questions:

- [ ] 1. Any blue-to-purple or indigo-to-violet gradient left, anywhere?
- [ ] 2. Any gradient text (`background-clip: text`)?
- [ ] 3. Does anything that is not a floating overlay (modal, popover, toast) have a shadow?
- [ ] 4. Any sparkle glyph (`✨`, `✦`, `🪄`)?
- [ ] 5. Any emoji used as interface?
- [ ] 6. Does any icon sit inside a tinted square, circle, or box?
- [ ] 7. Any em dash (`—`) in UI copy?
- [ ] 8. Any hits from the banned word list (*unleash, supercharge, seamless...*)?
- [ ] 9. Does each feature or category have its own decorative colour?
- [ ] 10. Does any button contain a moving arrow on hover?
- [ ] 11. Does anything glow, lift, or scale on hover?
- [ ] 12. Is there an eyebrow badge above the hero that says nothing?
- [ ] 13. Is the hero headline above 56px, or any section over 96px of vertical padding?
- [ ] 14. Does any element look oversized next to the text beside it?

**Rule:** If a reviewer could tell the page was generated by AI in under 5 seconds, find the specific tell and fix it.

---
